chunks: Surely, revolt and falsehood abase a man in his religious as well as worldly matters and manifest his shortcomings before his critic. You know that you cannot catch what is destined to remain away from you. Many people had aims other than right (ones) and began to swear by Allāh (that they will attain their goal) but He falsified them. Therefore, fear the Day when happy is he who made his end happy (by good actions) while repentant is he who allowed Satan to lead him and did not resist him.
ai.seo_question: What are the effects of arrogance and falsehood on a person's faith and worldly life according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this letter to Muawiya, Imam Ali employs the term 'al-baghy' (transgression/extravagance) to highlight Muawiya's specific political overreach, linking spiritual corruption directly to worldly instability. The reference to those who 'swore falsely' alludes to the historical context of the Battle of Siffin, where opposing factions invoked oaths to justify their claims, serving as a precursor to the final judgment. This passage underscores the Shia emphasis on *haqq* (truth) versus *batil* (falsehood), warning that allowing Satan to guide one's actions leads to eternal regret on the Day of Reckoning.
